_README: The script for this app's 'root is available, but not granted' video. Read by the shared scripts
in the `iboalali-apps` kit; see the `store-video` skill for the full shape and what each step verb
Its takes and cuts are filed under the storyboard's own path below Play Store/Video, so it cannot
The state this video is about is the one people write in about. The app can see that a root
manager is present and still be refused by it, and the message saying so reads, at a glance, like
the app is broken. It is not: one button away is the fix.
_locales: English only for now. Nothing here is a framework surface, so localeScope is 'app' and every
extra language is one caption set plus one `--locale <name>` run: no rootable image, no reboot.

_note: The promo's, unchanged. Taken from the launcher icon, which is the app's only real brand mark:
a white '#' on Material Deep Purple 500. See the promo storyboard for why it is deliberately
NOT the app's Material theme.

_zoom: The promo has no camera moves; this does, because its subject is a sentence rather than a green
tick. 'Root is available but this app has not been granted access' has to be read, and at the
size a phone-in-a-frame gives it, it is a grey smear.
Two levels, as in Hide Persistent Notification's how-tos and for the same reason: the recording
is about 650 canvas pixels wide in the vertical frame and about 410 in the horizontal one, so one
number would either barely move the vertical cut or swallow the horizontal.

_package: The DEBUG build, like the promo: the armed root result is BuildConfig.DEBUG-gated and no
emulator is rooted, so there is no other way to film this state.
That has a cost worth knowing before re-recording. `app/src/debug/res` renames the app to
'Basic Root Checker (Debug)' and overrides the splash drawable, and the title bar renders
app_name, so the resource overrides have to be neutralized on disk for the build being filmed:
The applicationId keeps its .debug suffix, which is invisible: nothing this journey films
_startInApp: The app is opened off camera, during reset, so the take begins on the app's own screen. The
promo does the opposite on purpose: its story starts with the question, and it launches on
camera. A how-to should start on the screen it is about to talk about.
demo_root arms the answer the FAB will give, so the recorded journey is the real one (checking
snackbar, spinner, result animation, outcome haptic) with only the outcome decided in advance.
demo_device_name and demo_device_model decide what the device card says. Without them it reads
'emulator' and 'emu64xa', which contradicts the Pixel bezel the capture is composited into and
does not match the promo. Arming a device also tells the app a recording is in progress, which
is what hides Settings' debug-only cards.

_note: The promo's bed. The same track across an app's videos is what makes them read as a set.
1300ms is a beat to read the device card before anything moves. The push goes to the control
about to be tapped, so the camera move and the press are one gesture, and the 400ms after it
lets the move settle before the marker ring arrives 500ms ahead of the finger.
1600ms covers the checking snackbar and the spinner, which the armed path runs in full.

caption.default:
Root is there,
but not allowed yet.

_note: The push onto the status area is the whole reason this video zooms. Two lines have to be
read: the message, and 'via Magisk' under it, which is what tells the viewer the app found a
manager and was refused by it rather than finding nothing.
A fixed focus point because the status text carries no tag and its wording is localized. 0.33
is the midpoint of the message and the provider line on a 1344x2992 screen. Re-measure with
`android layout --pretty` if the status area's layout changes.
The armed result governs this button as it governs the FAB, so the tap runs the app's real
request path and lands back on the same state. That is not a fudge: it is what a real device
does when the manager's prompt is dismissed. The app asks, and nothing changes.

caption.default:
Then approve it
in your root manager.

_note: The one beat this video cannot film. The prompt belongs to Magisk, KernelSU or APatch, none of
which exists on an unrooted emulator, and mocking one up would be wrong twice over: it is
another project's UI, against which the About screen already disclaims affiliation, and it
would show one manager's dialog to viewers using any of several.
So the caption says it instead. A caption is the video's own voice and is correct for every
manager. If a rooted recording device ever exists, this is the only scene that changes.
The trailing wait is the tail the end card fades in over, and the pull-back has to finish and
settle before the take stops: the recording is frozen on its LAST frame for the whole hold.
The promo's card, unchanged. Same app, same offer, same link.
